C. What is the nature of the fauna and flora beneath the Ross Ice Shelf?
1. What is the interaction between biological activity under the Ross Ice Shelf with that in adjacent waters?
2. What peculiar life forms inhabit this unique environment?
3. What is the nutrient flow under the shelf?
4. What contribution to the understanding of worldwide pollution levels can come from the study of the organisms found in this highly specialized environment?
5. How do special conditions beneath the ice shelf affect the biota and in turn the levels of CO<sub>2</sub> and oxygen in the water mass?
D. What is the history of the Ross Sea Embayment?
What are the conditions of sedimentation on the sea floor beneath the Ross Ice Shelf?
2. What can be learned from the sub-ice shelf environment that will aid in the understanding of marine tillites found in the geologic past?
3. How do the sediment and sedimentary conditions vary with distance from the ice front?
4. What is the form of the sea floor below the Ross Ice Shelf?
5. What is the sediment thickness? Sediment characteristics?
6. What magnetic signatures are present?
7. Are any major geologic structures present?
8. What fossils are present? Can these be used as temperature indicators?
9. What is the tectonic, volcanologic, and glacial history of the Ross Sea Area?
10. Is the sea floor beneath the Ross Ice Shelf in present isostatic balance?
The questions of worldwide significance are more difficult to pose as simple questions. It is evident, however, that the analysis of the Ross Ice Shelf ice cores and sediment cores from the sea floor below the ice shelf should provide information that will aid in the interpretation and understanding of the late Cenozoic climatic and glacial history, not only of the Antarctic but of the rest of the world.
